record.paper_title: Open Problems in Efficient Semi-Supervised PAC Learning
record.original_question: Beyond the concrete cases listed in the note, the broader open problem is to identify additional concept classes C and compatibility notions χ in the semi-supervised PAC model for which unlabeled data can be exploited by computationally efficient algorithms to reduce labeled sample complexity in the sense suggested by the compatibility-filtered search space.

evidence.quote: More generally, it would be interesting to consider other classes and notions of compatibility as well.
The high-level question is whether for interesting classes C and notions of compatibility χ, one can learn with this many (or polynomial in this many) labeled examples by efficient algorithms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Fix an instance space X and a concept class C of functions c : X → {0,1}. In the semi-supervised PAC learning model, a target concept c* ∈ C and an unknown distribution D over X are fixed. A learner receives two samples drawn i.i.d. from D: an unlabeled sample U of size m_u, and a labeled sample L of size m_l (each example in L is labeled by c*). Given ε, δ ∈ (0,1), the learner must output a hypothesis h with err_D(h) := Pr_{x ∼ D}[h(x) ≠ c*(x)] ≤ ε, with probability at least 1 − δ.

A compatibility notion is a function χ : C × Δ(X) → [0,1] (where Δ(X) is the set of distributions on X) that measures how compatible a hypothesis is with the marginal distribution D, with the assumption that χ(c*, D) is close to 1 (or above a known threshold τ). Given an unlabeled sample U, one defines an empirical compatibility χ̂(·, U), and the unlabeled-data-filtered version of the class is

  C_{χ,τ}(U) := { c ∈ C : χ̂(c, U) ≥ τ − γ }

for an appropriate slack γ. The labeled sample complexity in this filtered model can be bounded in terms of an effective complexity measure of C_{χ,τ}(U) (for example, its VC dimension or a uniform-convergence-based measure), which can be much smaller than the corresponding measure of C itself when χ is informative about D.

Problem. Exhibit additional pairs (C, χ) — beyond known examples — for which all of the following hold simultaneously:

1. There exists a non-trivial compatibility notion χ such that the χ-compatibility of c* with respect to D is bounded away from arbitrary by a known constant τ, and such that the effective complexity of C_{χ,τ}(U) is provably smaller than that of C (i.e., χ genuinely uses the unlabeled distribution to shrink the search space).

2. There is a computationally efficient algorithm (running in time polynomial in the relevant parameters, including 1/ε, 1/δ, and the description size of concepts in C) that, given an unlabeled sample of size polynomial in these parameters together with a labeled sample whose size matches (up to polynomial factors) the labeled sample complexity dictated by the effective complexity of C_{χ,τ}(U), outputs a hypothesis h with err_D(h) ≤ ε with probability at least 1 − δ.

3. In particular, the resulting labeled sample complexity is asymptotically smaller than the best known efficient supervised PAC learner for C, demonstrating that unlabeled data is provably leveraged by an efficient algorithm.

The task is to identify and analyze such new pairs (C, χ), or to prove obstructions to their existence under standard complexity-theoretic assumptions.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem as posed is a broad research direction asking for new efficient semi-supervised PAC learners with provable labeled-sample savings via compatibility notions. While individual special cases (e.g., for linear separators with margin compatibility, or certain co-training settings) have been studied since the introduction of the Balcan–Blum framework, the general question of identifying new (C, χ) pairs admitting efficient learners with reduced labeled complexity remains an ongoing research program with no comprehensive resolution. We did not find a single result that closes the broad problem.

status_evidence.title: A PAC-Style Model for Learning from Labeled and Unlabeled Data (Balcan & Blum)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces compatibility notions χ between concepts and distributions and shows reductions in labeled sample complexity when χ filters the hypothesis space.
status_evidence.claim: Framework defines compatibility-filtered hypothesis class and motivates the general open problem of finding new (C, χ) pairs with efficient algorithms.
